original_question: If G is a triangle-free planar graph, is its list packing number always at most 4? In other words, must chi*_l(G) <= 4 hold for every triangle-free planar graph G?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Various open problems related to list packing," subsection "Planar graphs," Problem 2.8: "For a triangle-free planar graph G, is it true that χ^⋆_ℓ(G)≤4?" ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target almost exactly: it uses the right graph class (triangle-free planar graphs), the right invariant (the list packing number χ^⋆_ℓ(G)), and the right bound (4). In substance, it is essentially Problem 2.8 stated in slightly expanded prose. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the notation χ^⋆_ℓ(G) should be unpacked: the paper defines it as the least integer k such that, for every k-list-assignment L of G, the graph admits an L-packing of size k. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

A list-assignment in the paper is a function L:V(G)→2^N, and a 4-list-assignment means that every vertex receives a 4-element list of colours. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

An L-colouring c must satisfy c(v)∈L(v) for every vertex v, and it is proper when adjacent vertices get different colours. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

Disjointness of colourings is vertexwise: for colourings c_i and c_j, one requires c_i(u)≠c_j(u) for every vertex u. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

The quantifier is over all triangle-free planar graphs G; the paper does not add extra assumptions such as connectedness, regularity, cubicity, or bipartiteness. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

The paper places this specifically in the "Planar graphs" part of Section 2, as a sharpening of recent upper-bound questions for planar graphs, so the refined question should stay exactly at the triangle-free planar level and not broaden to larger graph classes. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
refined_question: For every triangle-free planar graph G and every 4-list-assignment L on V(G) (with L(v) a 4-element subset of N for each v), do there exist four pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings c1,c2,c3,c4 of G, where each c_i(v)∈L(v), each c_i is proper, and c_i(v)≠c_j(v) for every vertex v and all i≠j? Equivalently, is χ^⋆_ℓ(G)≤4 for every triangle-free planar graph G? ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
justification: The official target is exactly Problem 2.8, not a broader neighboring question about all planar graphs (Problems 2.6 and 2.7) and not a different list-packing problem elsewhere in the paper. The only substantive improvement needed to make your draft fully self-contained is to spell out the paper’s definitions of k-list-assignment, proper L-colouring, disjointness, and χ^⋆_ℓ(G). Once those are included, the refined question is paper-faithful and essentially identical to the authors’ intended open problem. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
